description: A principal must approve the publication plan for a student newspaper investigation and finalize its attribution, distribution channel, image use, and records access, with input from the journalism adviser and the library media specialist.

shared_context.S1: The student newspaper has completed an investigative article about changes to the school's lunch program.
shared_context.S2: The draft names a student source and includes a photograph obtained from the school media bank.
shared_context.S3: The proposed publication package would publish the article in the printed newspaper and on the public school website, retain the named attribution, and keep the photograph with both versions.
shared_context.S4: Dr. Morgan gives final approval for student-publication plans.
shared_context.S5: As part of the school's normal pre-publication review, Dr. Morgan asks the journalism adviser and library media specialist to report any issue affecting publication, attribution, images, or records access.

PF1.text: The student source contacted Ms. Ellis after the draft was completed and explicitly requested the pseudonym "River" because the source is a minor concerned about retaliation; the adviser confirmed that the source's statement may be published only with that pseudonym, but the request has not yet been entered in the article file.

PF2.text: Mr. Shah checked the media-bank license for the photograph this week and confirmed that it permits use in the printed newspaper and the school's password-protected internal archive, but not on the public website; the license record has not yet been attached to the publication request.

acceptance_conditions: The article must be approved for publication.
The article must appear in the printed newspaper and not on the public website.
The source must be identified by the pseudonym River.
The photograph must remain in the print edition but be excluded from the public website.
The article record must be limited to the school's password-protected internal archive.
The settlement must include formal records for source protection and image-license compliance.

decisive_facts.why: The source's explicit request changes the byline from the named attribution in the draft to exactly "River" and requires a source-protection record.

The license terms change distribution from print plus public website to print only, remove the photograph from the website, restrict the archive to internal access, and require an image-license record.
